verdicts.evidence: An independent numerical audit checks the supporting-score identity for L1, L2, and KL on 99×100 grids, finding max oracle identity error and constant-target score of 0 and supporting-plane violations at machine precision (1.11e-16), confirming the constant 1-alpha predictor is unbeatable under perfect conditional coverage.

The logbook only re-aggregates the authors' released results.csv (not an independent run) and obtains 68.9% and 33.7%, which do not match the paper's claimed 68.4% and 38.3%; the PartitionWise value differs by ~4.6 percentage points with no explanation.

An independent synthetic experiment on the paper's 8D heteroscedastic model shows L1-ERT recovering 92% of the analytic violation (0.0866 vs 0.0948) at 30,000 test points while unaligned CovGap recovers only 5% (0.0049), with the convergence trend visible already at 3,000 samples.

The same 30,000-point synthetic run evaluates both clipped convex components, finding over-coverage 0.0445 (analytic 0.0460) and under-coverage 0.0464 (analytic 0.0488), both nonzero and close to theory.

The logbook only reads the authors' released classification CSV and checks additivity (residual 8.94e-8) and directional gaps; no classification experiments are independently executed, so this is a sanity check on released artifacts rather than experimental verification.

A mutation control with 20 seeds and 5 folds shows a label memorizer produces false in-sample ERT of 0.08886 but cross-fitted null ERT of 0, while a genuine two-region signal still yields cross-fitted ERT of 0.01013, directly demonstrating that k-fold cross-fitting removes overfitting artifacts without erasing real signal.

overall: The logbook provides solid independent experimental evidence for the metric identity foundations (C1), synthetic convergence behavior (C3), asymmetric decomposition (C4), and Algorithm 1 cross-fitting mechanism (C6). Claims C2 and C5 are unsupported because they merely re-aggregate or read the authors' own released data without running independent experiments, and C2's replayed numbers do not match the paper's Table 2 values.
